t: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, and the Chairman of the Farm Credit Administration shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed spending plan by program, project, and activity for the funds made available under this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that submitting a spending plan to committees is a formal consultative step. It fails because the Secretary of Agriculture, the FDA Commissioner, the Farm Credit Administration Chairman and the congressional Appropriations Committees are all inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed spending plan

qwen_block.w: The section requires federal officials to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is considered part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve outside parties. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed spending plan

opus.w: This section only requires federal officials to send a spending plan to congressional committees. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is a report within the government. It is not participation by states, tribes, experts, companies or the public. A submission requirement may look procedural, but it never crosses the federal boundary.
opus.s: shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed spending plan by program, project, and activity for the funds made available under this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The phrase "submit to the Committees on Appropriations" sounds like a formal step, so it's tempting to call it participation. That reading fails. The officials submitting the plan (Secretary of Agriculture, FDA Commissioner, Farm Credit Administration Chairman) are federal, and so are the people receiving it (congressional committees). No one outside the federal government is involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires federal officials to submit a spending plan to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an intra-governmental action. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any non-federal entities (such as states, tribes, or the public) in the creation or submission of this plan.
qwen_chat.s: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, and the Chairman of the Farm Credit Administration shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed spending plan by program, project, and activity for the funds made available under this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the plan is "detailed" and involves multiple agencies, it requires coordination or consultation with outside entities to create. However, the text only mandates the submission of a report to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, and the creation of an internal spending plan by federal agencies does not inherently require consulting with non-federal parties (states, public, etc.). Therefore, this is an internal administrative requirement, not participation.
